title: v1/chat.completions: role-mapper, stop-arbiter, and framed-JSON tool-handoff for parity
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds an OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility layer that normalizes param coercion, introduces a stop-sequence arbitration policy, role alias mapping, and a framed-JSON tool handoff for streaming function calls. Backwards-compatible by default; gated under v1_compat_mode for rollout.
description:
Motivation: customers using Redwood's OpenAI compatibility endpoint reported inconsistent behavior when mixing stop sequences, function calls, and role aliases across streams. This PR implements three orthogonal components to bring deterministic parity with common v1 expectations while keeping native runtime optimizations available.

Summary: implement a stop-sequence arbitrator (stop_precedence), a role-mapper to coalesce common role aliases (role_aliases + strict_role_mode opt-in), and a framed-JSON tool-handoff event so function calls in streaming mode are unambiguous and resilient to chunk boundaries. Also: normalize numeric/boolean param coercion for v1 requests and add e2e tests for overlapping stop/functioncall edge cases.

Key behavioral changes (enabled when request includes v1_compat_mode=true):
- stop_precedence (new request param): controls deterministic arbitration when multiple stop conditions occur in-flight (values: "first-token", "boundary-first", "function-priority"). Default for compatibility is "boundary-first" which prefers completed token boundaries and preserves OpenAI-like heuristics.
- Role-mapper: request-level role_aliases map common client roles (e.g., "user", "human", "end-user") to canonical roles. When strict_role_mode is true we return warnings for ambiguous role assignments and fall back to the mapper instead of failing.
- Framed-JSON tool-handoff: a small JSON envelope emitted as a discrete stream event when the model proposes a function call. Envelope fields are: event:"tool_handoff", tool:string, args:{...}, outgoing_signature:string. This avoids mid-chunk JSON parsing errors and provides a clear point for the runtime to execute tool calls or route to function execution layers.
- Logprobs and streaming offsets: logprob normalization was adjusted so per-token contributions are stable even when the stream fragments tokens across frames; a post-stream rebase step reconciles offsets and preserves reported token indices for v1 clients.

Files changed (high level): service/api/openai_compat/v1_handler.py, service/stream/framer.go, runtime/stop_arbiters/stop_arbiter.rs, docs/openai_compat.md, tests/integration/test_stop_function_interop.py, sdk/typescript/examples/v1_parity_chat.md, ci/compat_e2e.yml, tools/compat/role_aliases.yaml

Commits: See commits list below for granular change descriptions (squash merged).

Testing and rollout: added 10 new integration tests and 6 unit tests covering boundary-first vs function-priority arbitration, role alias collisions, and streaming handoff framing. This change is behind the HTTP compatibility flag v1_compat_mode to allow staged rollout; default behavior for non-v1 requests is unchanged.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: servers will accept both the old streaming envelope and the new framed-JSON event; SDKs updated to prefer framed events when v1_compat_mode is set. Documentation updates are included.

Merge notes: squash merge to main after CI green and two approvals.

Review conversation (condensed): see review_comments for threaded excerpts.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (review): The stop_arbitrator looks clean. Two items: ensure we never drop a functioncall event when a stop sequence spans the same tokens; add a unit test that simulates mid-token boundary fragmentation.
Asha (reply): Added the boundary-first strategy and the mid-token fragmentation e2e. The arbiter exposes a resolve_trace for telemetry so we can see which rule fired.
Riley Chen (review): Role-mapper is useful, but please document how SDKs should indicate role_aliases. Also we need a WARN-level log if strict_role_mode sees an ambiguous role.
Asha (reply): role_aliases.yaml added to tools/compat and SDK example updated. We emit a compat.warn metric when strict_role_mode fallback occurs.
Samira Khan (security review): framer.go looks good but confirm the framed JSON event size is bounded and validated to avoid amplification attacks.
Asha (reply): added a 64KB cap and JSON-schema validation for the tool_handoff envelope; validation failures close the stream with a 400 and compat error code.
Diego Martinez (approval): CI green, tests added. Approving for merge after squash.
